references.text: The prophecy of the Messiah who suffers for humanity's sins, bears their pain, and through whose wounds we receive healing, mirrors Jesus' call to take up his cross.
David's trust in God despite persecution and suffering reflects Jesus' call to self-denial and following him.
Luke repeats Jesus' words about denying oneself, taking up one's cross daily, and following him, which underscores the importance of this message.
Mark's version of Jesus' call to self-denial and bearing his cross shows the universality of this calling among the Synoptics.
Jesus' words about hating one's life in this world to keep it for eternal life resonate with the message of self-denial and following him.

The call to lay aside everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles, and to run the race of endurance with eyes fixed on Jesus, reflects the idea of self-denial and bearing one's cross.
